hero.title: Planning How The UpSkilling Labs Will Evolve
hero.summary: Logic model view of envisioned improvements to The UpSkilling Labs program and growth. Over time these improvements lend to shared knowledge and adaptable structures that can benefit new communities, volunteers, and learners.
hero.howToRead: Read left to right. Each column leads to the next: what we put in, what we do, what we can count, then what we intend to change within 12 months, in 1 to 3 years, and in 3 years or more. Every item names the workstream it belongs to. Choose a workstream to highlight its items.

items.text: Builders in residence, who give 4 to 6 hours a week to research and build.
Maintainers, who keep the work going between Build Cycles.
Learning content contributors, who create and share learning content.
Coding agents that handle clerical work so volunteers can do the thinking.
OLOS, The Labs' open-source platform, and the region's own copy of it.
GitHub, where research, code and records are kept in public.
Communication tools: Slack, Luma and email.
Records from past Build Cycles.
Learning content The Labs has already delivered.
Funding and other contributed resources.
Create an ecosystem map of The Labs.
Create a glossary of important terms.
Identify key learning content for different stages of user engagement.
Create an improved version of OLOS.
Make a plan for syncing multiple communication channels.
Make a plan for developing a standardized approach to content delivery.
Make a plan for developing the skillsets and training that new learning content contributors need.
Provide resources and lessons learned to builders in residence.
Recruit new volunteers.
Promote public events.
An ecosystem map of The Labs, published on GitHub.
A transferable glossary of key terms.
A list of key learning content for each stage of participant engagement.
An improved version of OLOS introduced to active participants.
A written plan for syncing communication channels.
A written plan for standardizing content delivery and training new learning content contributors.
A summary of lessons learned and feedback from first year build cycles.
An assessment of active volunteers and efforts to recruit and engage new volunteers.
A cycle of public events promoted and held, with similiar or increased attendance as first year.
Maintainers share one picture of the ecosystem and use the same words for it.
Participants know which learning content serves each stage of engagement.
Builders and Learners work with improved version of OLOS. Participant use, engagement, and data collected for analyses are evaluated against goals
The team has agreed plans for communication channels, content delivery and contributor training.
New volunteers join, and public events have suitable attendance.
Slack, Luma and email stay in sync, so people find the same information wherever they look.
Learning content contributors follow a standard approach, making use of instructional training as relevant.
Development of a single repository to hold and share learning content and process resources.
Regional groups and new Build Cycles make use of resources and are able to contribute data and feedback for continued learning and improvement.
Regional component of improved OLOS is transferable to new regions as they onboard.
New regions start own Upskilling Labs from shared tools and learning content.
A primarily volunteer-led way of upskilling that funders and partners can back with confidence.
A master repository holds The Upskilling Labs' learning content and process resources.
A self-service learning platform lets people find and use learning content on their own.

indicators.intro: Sample measures for each outcome horizon. These will change as the c04 team refines goals, objectives, and targets and confirms currently tracked information and baselines.

horizons.title: Short term
items: Maintainers agree the ecosystem map and glossary match how they see The Upskilling Labs.
Stages of engagement and respective learning content identified.
Improved OLOS is operational and active participants are testing.
Plans for efficient and effective communication put into action.
Plans for content delivery and contributor training approved and put into action mid-2027.
Targets for new maintainers, new participants (builders and learners), and public event attendees are established.

horizons.title: Medium term
items: Actively monitoring effectiveness of different communication channels, making adjustments as necessary.
Evaluated the standard approach to learning content, training for contributors, and new content created.
Actively monitoring participation and event attendance.
As new regions onboard, a regional OLOS is easily transferred with connection to shared resources.
Actively monitoring use of OLOS and participant feedback.
Any updates to OLOS are seamlessly pushed out to regional groups.

horizons.title: Long term
items: Learning content and process resources held in the master repository stay current and evolve as needed.
[#] people a month using the self-service learning platform.
[#] new regions starting from shared tools and lessons.
Share of The Labs' budget from [#] recurring funders and partners.

assumptions: Builders in residence, maintainers and learning content contributors can give enough time each Build Cycle to finish what they start.
Build Cycle records and delivered learning content are complete enough to build on.
Staff and volunteers will use one shared map, glossary and repository instead of keeping their own.
Slack, Luma, email and GitHub can be kept in sync with tools The Upskilling Labs can afford and maintain.
Learners will use self-service learning content when it is easy to find.
Other regions want to start from shared tools and lessons.
external: How fast AI tools change, and what they cost.
Volunteer capacity around jobs, family and the calendar.
Funding cycles and what funders are prioritizing.
Changes to the platforms relied on, such as GitHub, Slack and Luma.
